description:
Delete a post for good, removing it from the site if it was published. There is no undo; to only take it off the site use unpublish_post. Same as `micropage posts rm <slug>`.

Needs confirm: true, which you should only pass after the user has agreed. Deleting a slug that does not exist is not an error (deleted: false). Queues a site rebuild when a post was removed and the project has been published. The site rebuild redeploys the live build, so an unpublished page draft left by save_page or the editor stays a draft. It returns build_id and after_event_id to follow the rebuild with get_deploy_status.

confirm.description: Must be true. Ask the user first: the post is deleted for good and leaves the live site.

project.description: Which project: its uuid, its numeric id, its micropage hostname ("acme" or "acme.micropage.sh") or its custom domain ("www.acme.com"). A full URL also works. Get valid values from list_projects.

slug.description: The post's slug, as list_posts shows it (e.g. "launching-new-dashboard"). Normalised like the CLI does.

name: delete_post

after_event_id.description: Pass to get_deploy_status with build_id to see only events from this rebuild.

build_id.description: The build the site rebuild redeploys: the live one, not an unpublished page draft. Pass to get_deploy_status; null when nothing was rebuilt.

deleted.description: False when no post had that slug (nothing to delete).

rebuild_queued.description: True when a site rebuild of the live build was queued to take the post down.

title: Delete a micropage post
